chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, who said:
I saw Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and he had come out to me. So I began looking at him, and I continued to look at his head and his feet so that I might describe his stature to our companions in Miṣr.
While I was like that, he sat down and said: O ʿAlī, indeed Allah has argued concerning the Imamate with the like of that by which He argued concerning prophethood, so He said:
And We gave him judgment while yet a child.
And when he reached his maturity and reached forty years.
So it is permissible that wisdom be given to one while he is a child, and it is permissible that it be given to him while he is a son of forty years.

key_terms.النُّبُوَّةِ: prophethood as a parallel mode of divine proof
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةِ: the divinely appointed office of the Imam
key_terms.الْحُكْمَ: judgment or divinely granted wisdom and authority
key_terms.صَبِيًّا: while still a child or very young

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the possibility of an Imam receiving divine authority at a young age?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah establishes the proof for the Imamate in a manner comparable to prophethood. It shows that divine wisdom and authority may be granted at a young age or at forty years, and therefore age alone does not invalidate the appointment of an Imam.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Asbat who said,

‘I saw Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and he<sup>asws</sup> had come out to me. So I took to looking at him<sup>asws</sup> and went on looking at him<sup>asws</sup> to his<sup>asws</sup> head and his<sup>asws</sup> legs in order to be able to describe him<sup>asws</sup> to our companions in Egypt.

While I was during that, he<sup>asws</sup> sat down and said: ‘O Ali! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Argued regarding the Imamate similar to what He<sup>azwj</sup> Argued with regarding the Prophet-hood, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Said
[19:12] and We Granted him the Wisdom whilst he was a child.
[46:15] until when he attains his maturity and reaches forty years.

Thus, it is allowed that he<sup>as</sup> be Given the Wisdom and he<sup>as</sup> was a child, and it is allowed that He<sup>azwj</sup> be Given it and he<sup>as</sup> was a man of forty years of age’.
en.sarwar: 7. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Asbat who has said the following.
“Once I saw abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who had come out to me and I began to look at him from head to his toes so I can describe him to our people in Egypt.

I was looking until he sat down and said, “O Ali, Allah has supported His argument against the people in the case of Imamat (Leadership with Divine Authority) just as He has done so in the case of the prophets. He has said,
“We gave authority to him (John) over the people during his childhood [19:12].. When he attained maturity, God gave him strength, wisdom and knowledge. Thus, do We reward those who do good.” [12:22]
“When he grew-up to manhood and became forty years old,. .” [46:15].
It come to pass that wisdom comes to a prophet when he is just a child or it may come to a prophet when he is forty years old.”
